items.context: With 500 violations across 604 files, the approach matters. Incremental means tackling files one-by-one with tidiness-manager recommendations, validating tests after each. Batch means grouping by violation type (all long_files first, then complex_functions, then lint) and processing in sweeps.

options.label: Incremental per-file (tidiness-manager driven)
options.rationale: Lower risk per change, easier to review, but slower overall. tidiness-manager prioritizes by composite score.

options.label: Batch by violation type
options.rationale: More efficient — handle all long_files in one pass, then complexity, then lint. Matches the natural phasing in the plan. Recommended because the violations are well-categorized and independent.

options.label: Hybrid: batch by type, but validate incrementally
options.rationale: Process one violation type at a time, but run tests after every 5-10 files. Balances speed with safety.

items.context: No .golangci.yml exists. This is the biggest gap for the lint_issues category (24 violations). The level of strictness determines how many new issues surface and how much fix effort is needed.

options.label: Minimal: go vet + errcheck + unused only
options.rationale: Catches critical issues without noise. Low fix effort but may not move the needle enough on quality score.

options.label: Moderate: add gocritic, gocyclo, funlen, revive
options.rationale: Directly targets the violation categories (complex_functions via gocyclo, long_files via funlen). Recommended because it aligns linting with the exact GCT violation categories.

options.label: Strict: full golangci-lint preset with all major linters
options.rationale: Maximum coverage but will surface hundreds of issues beyond the 24 lint violations, potentially derailing the effort.

items.context: Some large files are data-driven (errors.go at 1,874 lines with 51+ error codes, mocks.go at 1,035 lines auto-generated). These inflate the long_files count but refactoring them is different from splitting logic-heavy files.

options.label: Exclude generated files, split data files by domain
options.rationale: Skip mocks.go (auto-generated), split errors.go into domain-specific error files (pipeline_errors.go, smoketest_errors.go, etc.). Recommended because it reduces long_files count without touching generated code.

options.label: Exclude both generated and data-heavy files from metrics
options.rationale: Mark errors.go and mocks.go as excluded via tidiness-manager. Fastest path but doesn't actually improve the code.

options.label: Refactor everything including generated files
options.rationale: Re-generate mocks with smaller interfaces, restructure errors. Thorough but high effort for marginal quality gain.

items.context: Many of the largest files are test files (service_test.go at 2,433 lines, supervisor_test.go at 1,544 lines, etc.). Test files contribute to long_files violations but splitting them requires care to maintain test helper sharing.

options.label: Split test files by function/scenario under test
options.rationale: E.g., smoketest_service_create_test.go, smoketest_service_run_test.go. Clear organization, but many new files.

options.label: Extract test helpers into testutil files, keep test files as-is
options.rationale: Reduces some length by extracting shared setup, but won't bring most files below threshold.

options.label: Split large test files + extract shared helpers
options.rationale: Split files over threshold by logical grouping AND extract common helpers into *_testutil_test.go. Recommended because it addresses both length and reuse.

items.text: The scenario already has 11 passing tests and 0 failures. All existing tests must continue to pass after refactoring. The GCT review also flagged 8 standards warnings (missing test files in runtime/infra and runtime/testutil, UI component issues) which are separate from the 500 code quality violations but could be addressed opportunistically.

plan_updates: Created initial plan.md scaffold with all 13 mandatory sections. Phases outlined (lint setup → long files → complexity → validate). Problem clarity is strong from GCT evidence. Approach details are pending decisions on strategy, lint strictness, and file handling.
